title: Platform detected
question: Which platform serves the store?
method: Informational. Detect WooCommerce (wc/store in the REST index, a woocommerce body class or generator), Shopify (cdn.shopify.com assets or the Shopify generator) or plain WordPress from the home page. The result selects the profile and the platform-specific checks; it is never scored.

title: Store API reachable
question: Can an agent read products through the Store API without credentials?
method: GET /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=1. Pass on 200 with a JSON array; fail on 401, 403, 404 or a non-JSON body.

title: Store API not rate-limited for reads
question: Do a few sequential Store API reads succeed?
method: Three sequential product list requests. Fail on any 429 or 5xx; warn when a Retry-After header appears, or when a read succeeded only on the scanner's single retry after a 429 or 503 (the Store API throttled the scanner once and recovered after Retry-After).

title: Store API product completeness
question: Do Store API products carry the fields an agent needs?
method: Sampled products must carry name, prices, images, stock status, permalink and categories. Pass when all do; warn when some lack images or categories; fail when prices or stock status are missing.

title: Public product feed discoverable
question: Can an agent reach the catalog as a feed without an account?
method: Look for a feed URL in link rel=alternate tags of the home page (RSS, Atom, XML or JSON types), in llms.txt, in robots.txt comments and Sitemap lines, and in the sitemap index (feed paths and data files only, never a product page whose slug contains the word); fetch the first candidate. Pass when it is a Google-format XML feed (g: namespace), a CSV or TSV with id (or item_id or sku), title, link (or url) and price columns, or JSON items with the same fields; an OpenAI-format feed (item_id or sku, url or link, image_url or image_link) is recognised and recorded as such. Fail when none is found. Every shopping surface ingests feeds pushed through its own channel and none documents reading a merchant-hosted URL, so a public copy is a convenience for agents, not a requirement: weight 1. The specifications are cited for the formats only.

spec.title: Google Merchant Center product data specification

title: Feed freshness
question: Was the feed updated recently?
method: Read Last-Modified on the feed response or a timestamp inside the feed. Pass within 24 hours; warn within 7 days; fail beyond. The thresholds are this scanner's heuristic; no channel publishes one.

title: Catalog in sitemap matches Store API
question: Do the sitemap and the Store API agree on catalog size?
method: Compare the product URL count in the sitemap with the X-WP-Total header of the Store API product list. Pass within 10 percent; warn within 25 percent; fail beyond.

title: Shopify products.json readable
question: Can an agent read a Shopify catalog as JSON?
method: GET /products.json?limit=5. Pass on 200 with a products array; fail on 404, 401, a password page or HTML (the endpoint is disabled, the store is password-protected or headless); inconclusive (skipped) on 429, because Shopify rate-limits this endpoint per IP after a few requests. The endpoint is an undocumented but long-standing convention of every Online Store theme (the documented per-product form is /products/<handle>.js); Shopify's generated robots.txt and agents.md now point agents at the UCP catalog on /api/ucp/mcp instead, which B5.8 covers, so this check carries weight 2 and B5.8 counts as a readable catalog for Level 2. A headless storefront that only loads Shopify assets is skipped as not applicable: Shopify serves neither products.json nor the UCP endpoint on that domain.
